intro: If you've spent another Midlothian winter with cold tiles underfoot and a heating bill that doesn't match the warmth you're getting, you're not alone. Plenty of homeowners in Borthwickhead are making the move to underfloor heating — and it's easy to see why. Whether you're renovating a period cottage or fitting out a new extension on a modern estate property, underfloor heating offers a level of comfort and efficiency that traditional radiators simply can't match. It heats rooms evenly from the ground up, frees up wall space, and when properly installed and zoned, can genuinely reduce your energy costs over time. This page covers everything you need to know before getting started.
localContext: Borthwickhead sits in a part of Midlothian where the housing stock is genuinely varied, and that matters a great deal when planning underfloor heating. Older stone-built properties and period cottages — common throughout the area — present specific challenges. Stone floors and solid ground floors require a wet system with a screed pour, which adds time and cost but delivers excellent long-term performance. Suspended timber floors in older homes can accommodate electric or low-profile wet systems, though proper insulation beneath the floor is essential to avoid heat loss downward rather than upward. On Borthwickhead's more modern estates, properties with newer concrete slabs are often the most straightforward to retrofit. It's also worth noting that Borthwickhead sits in a moderately hard water area. For wet underfloor heating systems, this means using inhibitor fluid and fitting a good filter is important to prevent scale build-up in the manifold and pipework over time — something an experienced local installer will factor in from the outset.
serviceDetail: A professional underfloor heating installation in Borthwickhead typically follows a clear sequence of steps, and knowing what to expect helps you plan around it. The process begins with a site survey, where an installer assesses your floor construction, existing boiler or heat source, room dimensions, and insulation levels. This visit shapes the system design — how many zones you need, pipe spacing, manifold location, and whether your boiler can handle the additional load or needs upgrading. For wet systems, which are the most popular choice for whole-house installations in Borthwickhead, flexible pipe is laid in a continuous loop across insulation boards on the subfloor. The manifold — a control hub that distributes water to each zone — is typically fitted in a cupboard or utility area. Once pipework is pressure-tested, a self-levelling screed is poured over the top. This needs to cure fully before the heating is commissioned, which usually takes several weeks depending on conditions. During commissioning, the system is slowly brought up to temperature in stages to avoid cracking the screed — a process called 'slow heat-up'. Electric underfloor heating, better suited to single rooms or areas with timber floors, is quicker to install but costs more to run day-to-day. Throughout the installation, a good tradesperson will keep disruption manageable, particularly in occupied homes, and will leave you with a clear guide to using your new system and thermostat controls.
pricing: In Borthwickhead, a full wet underfloor heating installation typically costs between £3,500 and £8,000, depending on the size and complexity of the project. A single-room wet system in a kitchen extension might come in at the lower end, while a whole-ground-floor installation in a larger period property with screed, insulation, manifold, and boiler upgrades could reach the upper range. Older stone-built properties often add cost due to floor preparation work and the need for additional insulation. Electric systems for a bathroom or utility room are more modest, typically £500–£1,200 fitted. Always get at least two detailed quotes that break down materials, labour, and any screed or groundwork costs separately.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickhead and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely makes a difference with a job like this. Local installers will have hands-on experience with the mix of property types here — they'll know the quirks of older stone-built homes, understand how suspended timber floors behave in this climate, and will be familiar with the water conditions that affect system longevity. They're also easier to reach if anything needs attention after the job is done. A premium installation like underfloor heating deserves someone who'll still be available for a follow-up call six months down the line, not a contractor who's moved on to the next area.

faqs.q: Is underfloor heating suitable for the older stone-built properties found in Borthwickhead?
faqs.a: Yes, though it requires more planning. Solid stone or concrete floors are well-suited to wet screed systems, provided adequate insulation is laid first to direct heat upward. Suspended timber floors in older cottages can use low-profile wet systems or electric mats. A proper survey of your floor construction is essential before committing to a system type.

faqs.q: How long does installation take for a typical Borthwickhead home?
faqs.a: For a whole ground-floor wet system, expect the physical installation to take three to five days, followed by a screed curing period of four to six weeks before the heating can be fully commissioned. Single-room electric systems are much quicker — often completed in a day. Your installer should give you a realistic project timeline during the survey visit.

faqs.q: Does the moderately hard water in Borthwickhead affect underfloor heating systems?
faqs.a: It can do over time. Hard water encourages limescale build-up in pipework and manifolds, which reduces efficiency. A reputable installer will add corrosion inhibitor fluid to the system, fit a magnetic filter, and advise on annual checks. This is straightforward to manage and shouldn't put you off — it's just a maintenance factor worth being aware of from day one.

faqs.q: Can I add underfloor heating to just one room in my Borthwickhead home rather than the whole ground floor?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Many homeowners in Borthwickhead start with a kitchen, bathroom, or extension before considering wider installation. A single-zone wet system or electric system for one room is a much smaller investment and a good way to experience underfloor heating before committing further. Just ensure the manifold position is planned with future expansion in mind if you think you'll extend the system later.
